nodes.summary: `ω` agrees with `ψ` on every edge outside `F`.
nodes.title: Agreement of configurations off an edge set

nodes.summary: The edge parameters `p_e(β) = 1 - exp (-β J_e)`.
nodes.title: Edge parameters $p_e(\beta) = 1 - e^{-\beta J_e}$

nodes.summary: The logarithmic `β`-derivative of the random-cluster weight under `betaParams`: `∑_{e ∈ E(G)} (J_e / p_e) (𝟙[e open] - p_e)`.
nodes.title: Logarithmic $\beta$-derivative of the random-cluster weight

nodes.summary: A symmetry of `ℤ^d` that preserves nearest-neighbour adjacency and every centered box `Λ_n = [-n, n]^d`, such as a coordinate reflection or a coordinate permutation.
nodes.title: Box symmetry of $\mathbb{Z}^d$

nodes.summary: The finite-energy constant `min (p / (p + q (1 - p))) (1 - p)`.
nodes.title: Finite-energy constant of the random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: The number `c(ω)` of closed edges of `G` in `ω`.
nodes.title: Number of closed edges

nodes.summary: The fibre of configurations agreeing with `ψ` off `F`.
nodes.title: Fibre of configurations agreeing off an edge set

nodes.summary: Conditioned on the states of the edges outside `F`, the random-cluster measure is the FK weight renormalized on the fibre (Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model*, 2006, Lemma 4.13).
nodes.title: Domain Markov property (finite volume)

nodes.summary: The random-cluster measure conditioned on agreeing with `ψ` off `F`.
nodes.title: Random-cluster measure conditioned on the edges off a set

nodes.summary: The conditional probability under `φ_{G,p,q}` that `e` is open given the states of all other edges: `φ(setOpen e ω) / (φ(setOpen e ω) + φ(setClosed e ω))`.
nodes.title: Conditional probability that an edge is open given the rest

nodes.summary: The event that `x` and `y` are joined by a path of open edges of `G`.
nodes.title: Event that two vertices are joined by open edges

nodes.summary: The real-valued state `𝟙[e open]` of the edge `e`.
nodes.title: Real-valued indicator that an edge is open

nodes.summary: Membership in `B` depends only on the states of edges outside `F`.
nodes.title: Event depending only on edges outside a set

nodes.summary: The inhomogeneous Bernoulli product `∏_{e ∈ E(G)} (pf e if e open, 1 - pf e if closed)`.
nodes.title: Inhomogeneous Bernoulli edge product

nodes.summary: The inhomogeneous Bernoulli product over the edges of `G` other than `e₀`.
nodes.title: Inhomogeneous Bernoulli product over all edges but one

nodes.summary: The Bernoulli edge product `∏_{e ∈ E(G)} (p if e open, 1 - p if e closed)`.
nodes.title: Bernoulli edge product

nodes.summary: The Bernoulli product over the edges of `G` other than `e`.
nodes.title: Bernoulli product over the edges other than one edge

nodes.summary: Representatives of the fibres of `F`: configurations with every edge of `F` closed.
nodes.title: Fibre representatives with every edge of a set closed

nodes.summary: Finite-energy property of the random-cluster measure. For `p ∈ (0, 1)` and `q ≥ 1`, the conditional probability that an edge is open given all other edges lies in `[cFE p q, 1 - cFE p q]`. For edges of `G` the sharper bounds `p / (p + q (1 - p))` and `p` are proved along the way. See G. Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 3.
nodes.title: Finite-energy property

nodes.summary: The covariance `E[f g] - E[f] E[g]` under the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure (a finite form of Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.covariance`).
nodes.title: Covariance under the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: The expectation `φ_{G,p,q}[X] = ∑_ω φ_{G,p,q}(ω) X(ω)` of an observable `X`.
nodes.title: Random-cluster expectation of an observable

nodes.summary: The expectation of `g` under the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure.
nodes.title: Expectation under the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: The unnormalized expectation `∑_ω g(ω) fkWeightW G pf q ω`.
nodes.title: Unnormalized inhomogeneous random-cluster expectation

nodes.summary: The ambient extension of the random-cluster edge law as a `PMF` on all `Sym2 V` configurations, with independent uniform bits on loops and nonedges.
nodes.title: Ambient random-cluster law as a probability mass function

nodes.summary: The inhomogeneous random-cluster probability `fkWeightW / fkZW`.
nodes.title: Inhomogeneous random-cluster probability

nodes.summary: The probability of the event `A` under the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure.
nodes.title: Probability of an event under the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: The probability of an ambient configuration: `fkWeight G p q ω / fkZ G p q`. For `0 < p < 1` and `q > 0`, its graph-edge marginal is the random-cluster law and unused coordinates are uniform.
nodes.title: Probability of an ambient FK configuration

nodes.summary: Under the free FK measure, the edges `e` and `σ e` are open with the same probability.
nodes.title: Graph automorphisms preserve free FK edge marginals

nodes.summary: Under the wired FK measure, the edges `e` and `σ e` are open with the same probability.
nodes.title: Boundary-preserving automorphisms preserve wired FK edge marginals

nodes.summary: Graph automorphisms preserve the free FK probability. See also `fvs_fkProb_reCfgIso` for isomorphisms between two graphs.
nodes.title: Graph automorphisms preserve the free FK probability

nodes.summary: Box symmetries preserve the free `q = 2` infinite-volume edge density. See also `rot_free_density_boxSym` for the statement on edges of `ℤ^d`.
nodes.title: Box symmetries preserve the free $q = 2$ density of box edges

nodes.summary: An automorphism `σ` of `G` is a graph isomorphism from the open subgraph of the relabelled configuration `reCfg σ ω` to the open subgraph of `ω`.
nodes.title: Automorphism as an isomorphism of open subgraphs

nodes.summary: The reflection `x ↦ x` with the `j`-th coordinate negated.
nodes.title: Reflection of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in one coordinate

nodes.summary: The reflection in the `j`-th coordinate as a box symmetry.
nodes.title: Coordinate reflection as a box symmetry

nodes.summary: Box symmetries preserve the wired `q = 2` infinite-volume edge density. See also `rot_wired_density_boxSym` for the statement on edges of `ℤ^d`.
nodes.title: Box symmetries preserve the wired $q = 2$ density of box edges

nodes.summary: Graph automorphisms preserving the boundary preserve the wired FK probability.
nodes.title: Boundary-preserving automorphisms preserve the wired FK probability

nodes.summary: An automorphism `σ` of `G` preserving the boundary set is a graph isomorphism between the wired graphs (open edges plus all boundary pairs) of `reCfg σ ω` and `ω`.
nodes.title: Boundary-preserving automorphism as an isomorphism of wired graphs

nodes.summary: At `q = 1` the random-cluster weight is the Bernoulli product weight.
nodes.title: At $q = 1$ the random-cluster weight is the Bernoulli product

nodes.summary: The inhomogeneous random-cluster weight `edgeProductW G pf ω · q ^ k(ω)`.
nodes.title: Inhomogeneous random-cluster weight

nodes.summary: The unnormalized random-cluster weight `p ^ o(ω) (1 - p) ^ c(ω) q ^ k(ω)`.
nodes.title: Unnormalized random-cluster weight

nodes.summary: The ambient FK normalizer, summing over every bit assignment on `Sym2 V`. Each loop or nonedge contributes a factor of two relative to the edge partition function `ecz_fkZEdge` defined in `EdgePartitionFunction`.
nodes.title: Ambient FK normalizer

nodes.summary: The partition function of the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure.
nodes.title: Partition function of the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: The wired and free FK edge marginals on the translated box `v + Λ_m` are the marginals on the centered box `Λ_m`, transported by `x ↦ x + v`.
nodes.title: Translation covariance of FK edge marginals on boxes

nodes.summary: Graph isomorphisms transport the wired and the free FK edge marginals: `σ e` is open in `H` with the same probability as `e` in `G`.
nodes.title: Boundary-matching isomorphisms transport FK edge marginals

nodes.summary: Isomorphic graphs have the same free FK probability, up to relabelling by the isomorphism. See also `fkTI_fkProb_reCfg`, the special case of an automorphism.
nodes.title: Isomorphic graphs have equal free FK probabilities after relabelling

nodes.summary: An isomorphism `σ : G ≃ H` is a graph isomorphism from the open subgraph of the pulled-back configuration `reCfgIso σ ω` to the open subgraph of `ω`.
nodes.title: Open-subgraph isomorphism for a pulled-back configuration

nodes.summary: For a permutation `σ` of `V`, pulling back along `σ` is the relabelling `reCfg σ`.
nodes.title: Pull-back along a permutation is relabelling

nodes.summary: The vertex boundary of `v + Λ_m`: the translate of the vertex boundary of `Λ_m`.
nodes.title: Vertex boundary of a translated box

nodes.summary: The nearest-neighbour graph of `ℤ^d` restricted to `v + Λ_m`.
nodes.title: Nearest-neighbour graph on a translated box

nodes.summary: For `d ≥ 1`, some translated box `v + Λ_m` is not contained in `Λ_m`, so translation is not a box symmetry in the sense of `BoxSym`.
nodes.title: Some translated box leaves the centered box for $d \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The vertices of the translated box `v + Λ_m`, as a subtype of `ℤ^d`.
nodes.title: Vertex type of a translated box

nodes.summary: The translated box `v + Λ_m = {y ∈ ℤ^d : ‖y - v‖_∞ ≤ m}`.
nodes.title: Translated box in $\mathbb{Z}^d$

nodes.summary: The translation `x ↦ x + v` from the centered box `Λ_m` onto `v + Λ_m`.
nodes.title: Translation from the centered box onto a translated box

nodes.summary: Isomorphic graphs with matching boundary sets have the same wired FK probability, up to relabelling. See also `fkTI_wiredFkProb_reCfg`.
nodes.title: Boundary-matching isomorphisms preserve wired FK probabilities

nodes.summary: An isomorphism `σ : G ≃ H` matching the boundary sets is a graph isomorphism between the wired graphs of `reCfgIso σ ω` and `ω`.
nodes.title: Wired-graph isomorphism for a pulled-back configuration

nodes.summary: Differential formula in `β` for the random-cluster measure with edge parameters `1 - exp (-β J_e)`: `d/dβ φ_β[g] = ∑_e (J_e / p_e) Cov(g, 𝟙[e open])`. See G. Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 3.
nodes.title: Differential formula in `β`

nodes.summary: Differential formula for the random-cluster measure: the derivative of `φ[g]` in the parameter of the edge `e₀` is `Cov(g, 𝟙[e₀ open]) / (p (1 - p))` with `p = pf e₀`. See G. Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 3.
nodes.title: Differential formula

nodes.summary: The derivative of the edge parameter `p(β) = 1 - exp (-β J)` is `J exp (-β J)`.
nodes.title: Derivative in $\beta$ of the edge parameter $1 - e^{-\beta J}$

nodes.summary: The FK measure induced on the fibre `condFibre F ψ`: FK weight divided by the fibre's total weight.
nodes.title: FK measure induced on a fibre

nodes.summary: The total FK weight of the fibre `condFibre F ψ`.
nodes.title: Total FK weight of a fibre

nodes.summary: The restriction of a box symmetry to a permutation of the vertices of the box `Λ_n`.
nodes.title: Restriction of a box symmetry to a box

nodes.summary: Opening an edge lowers the number of clusters by at most one.
nodes.title: Opening an edge lowers the cluster count by at most one

nodes.summary: Opening an edge does not increase the number of clusters. This is a special case of Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.card_le_card_of_le`, which proves it.
nodes.title: Opening an edge does not increase the cluster count

nodes.summary: The number `k(ω)` of open clusters: connected components of the open subgraph, isolated vertices included.
nodes.title: Number of open clusters

nodes.summary: The number `o(ω)` of open edges of `G` in `ω`.
nodes.title: Number of open edges

nodes.summary: The open subgraph is `G ⊓ fromEdgeSet {e | ω e = true}` in Mathlib's terms.
nodes.title: Open subgraph as the meet of $G$ with the open-edge graph

nodes.summary: The open subgraph is monotone in the configuration. The same statement is `StatMech.Sharpness.openSub_mono` in `BkCriterion`.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the open subgraph in the configuration

nodes.summary: Off the edges of `G`, flipping `e` does not change the open subgraph.
nodes.title: Toggling a non-edge leaves the open subgraph unchanged

nodes.summary: The open subgraph of `G` under the edge configuration `ω`: the edges of `G` that `ω` declares open.
nodes.title: Open subgraph of an edge configuration

nodes.summary: The configuration that closes every edge of `F` and agrees with `ψ` elsewhere.
nodes.title: Closing the edges of a set in a configuration

nodes.summary: Relabelling by `σ` as a permutation of the configuration space, with inverse relabelling by `σ⁻¹`.
nodes.title: Relabelling as a permutation of the configuration space

nodes.summary: Pull-back along `σ` as an equivalence of configuration spaces, with inverse the pull-back along `σ⁻¹`.
nodes.title: Pull-back of configurations as an equivalence

nodes.summary: The pull-back of a configuration `ω` on the edges of `W` along `σ : V ≃ W`: the edge `e` is open in `reCfgIso σ ω` iff `σ e` is open in `ω`. For `V = W` it is `reCfg` (`fvs_reCfgIso_eq_reCfg`).
nodes.title: Pull-back of an edge configuration along a vertex bijection

nodes.summary: The configuration `ω ∘ σ` on edges: the edge `e` is open in `reCfg σ ω` iff `σ e` is open in `ω`. See also `reCfgIso`, the same relabelling along an equivalence `V ≃ W`.
nodes.title: Relabelling of an edge configuration by a vertex permutation

nodes.summary: The tilt factor `λ = p₂ (1 - p₁) / ((1 - p₂) p₁)`, the ratio of the odds of an open edge at `p₂` and at `p₁`.
nodes.title: Tilt factor between two edge parameters

nodes.summary: FKG for connection events: for `q ≥ 1`, `φ(x ↔ y) φ(u ↔ v) ≤ φ(x ↔ y, u ↔ v)`.
nodes.title: FKG inequality for connection events for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The two-point function of the free random-cluster measure on a finite graph: the probability `φ(x ↔ y)` that `x` and `y` are connected by open edges.
nodes.title: Two-point function of the free random-cluster measure

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
